marks.gloss_en: a barrel that broke: one may rescue from it food for three meals
מאי טעמא? -- כיון דלסחיטה נינהו יהיב דעתיה: since olives and grapes are for squeezing, he sets his mind [on it], so R' Yehuda concedes there
Shmuel: R' Yehuda conceded to the Sages regarding olives and grapes -- [on his view, what comes out of them is forbidden]
one may not soak up wine
woman's milk, made only for infants, renders susceptible willed or unwilled; animal's milk, made for infants and adults -- is it not logical that it renders susceptible willed or unwilled?
the Sages (אמרו לו): if a woman's milk renders susceptible unwilled, that is because the blood of her wound is impure; shall animal milk, whose wound's blood is pure?
דתניא -- the baraita sets R' Yehuda (mulberries and pomegranates for food: permitted) against the Rabbis (forbidden), and has R' Yehuda forbid olives and grapes either way
olives from which one drew oil and grapes from which one drew wine, brought in whether for food or for liquid -- what comes out of them is forbidden

וסבר רבי יהודה סתם אסור? והתנן -- the milk mishna's baskets of olives and grapes: unwilled seepage does not render susceptible; if that means the unspecified case, then a fortiori for mulberries and pomegranates (kv_salim_tutim)
a woman's milk renders susceptible [to impurity] whether willed or unwilled
R' Yehuda would concede to the Rabbis on olives and grapes [what seeps from them is forbidden even if brought in for food]
R' Yirmeya to R' Abba: then about what do they disagree?
